items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after 33 years; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and runs the first earnings call since the transition on Nov 17 — the quarter Visible Alpha consensus expected to clear $108 billion in revenue
items.summary: Nvidia announced on November 12, 2026 that founder and CEO Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO, and director, effective immediately; the board recorded the resignation and appointments as of November 11, 2026 in a Form 8-K. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO while retaining her EVP and CFO roles; Harvey C. Jones became Nvidia's first-ever board chair. The press release does not state a reason; reporting from HotHardware, letsdatascience, and Kiplinger tied the exit to Huang's November 8 message to employees acknowledging infidelity, followed by reporting of a second relationship with another employee. Nvidia scheduled its Q3 fiscal 2027 earnings call for Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET, with Colette Kress providing written CFO commentary beforehand — the first Nvidia earnings call in 33 years not led by Huang. The quarter ended October 25, 2026; Visible Alpha consensus heading in was total revenue of roughly $108.7B, or +90.7% year over year, and S&P Global's November 12 preview estimated data center revenue near $101.8B, up from $89B in Q2 FY27 (reported October 2026). The board is expected to consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor. Names surfaced in press coverage include AMD's Lisa Su, Arm's Rene Haas, Apple CEO Tim Cook (publicly endorsed by President Trump), and Kress as an internal candidate — all speculation at this stage, not board decisions. Context: this run could not retrieve the November 17 post-close results directly — nvidia.com, investor.nvidia.com, and most financial-newswire primary domains remain DNS-blocked from this egress — so the headline numbers from the call itself are not yet in this snapshot and may land in tonight's enrichment.
items.why_it_matters: This is the biggest AI-industry structural story of November and was systematically missed by every prior digest run (Nov 12 pm through Nov 18 am) — referenced only as a dependent clause in today's BIS remote-access rule item ('days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure') but never as its own entry. Four threads worth pulling out. First, the leadership lineage: Huang built Nvidia from a graphics-chip startup into the dominant supplier of AI training and inference compute — Blackwell, Rubin, Vera Rubin, the DGX and HGX platforms, Isaac GR00T, NVLink, CUDA, and the entire data-center GPU category effectively ran through his personal operating cadence. An interim CFO-as-CEO configuration is a holding pattern, not a plan; the real signal is who the board names permanently and over what time horizon. The Kress-plus-Jones setup is the stand-in. Second, the operating-continuity test is literally this week. Q3 FY27 is the quarter where the data-center line was expected to clear $100B in a single three-month window for the first time, and the Blackwell ramp is the revenue engine Huang personally sold to every hyperscaler. The November 17 call is the first public read on whether the commercial pipeline runs without his pitch — the written CFO commentary is Kress's way of doing it without the usual Huang keynote-style delivery. Third, the strategic timing is tight. The BIS remote-access rule (in today's am as Tier-2) was issued five days after the resignation; California's agentic-containment lawsuit (today's am Tier-3) and the GPT-6.2 Astra 'High' self-improvement rating (today's am Tier-1) landed in the same week. Every one of those stories assumes Nvidia compute is the substrate, and the substrate just changed its top operator. For anyone forecasting AI build-out — hyperscaler capex, lab compute access, open-weight model training economics — Nvidia's post-Huang execution is the single biggest variable through 2027. Fourth, for Gabe's Python stack this is far-field, but it's worth tracking as a signal of market structure. Three concrete consequences to watch over the next 30 days: (a) does the Q3 print match the $108B consensus (if yes, the Kress-led execution thesis holds; if no, there's a real governance problem on top of the leadership problem); (b) does a permanent CEO get named on a specific timeline, or does the board slow-play it; (c) do hyperscaler contracts renew at the same pace they did under Huang. Each answer directly changes the compute cost curve that every PyTorch, llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang workload depends on.
